fixDescription.defect: rebuild_issued_by built its expected-issuer map from identifier_index rows of type cik. Production holds ZERO such rows (migration 0058 unapplied), so expected_issuer was always None, the agreement branch was unreachable, and all 147 disagreements carried expected_issuer_node_id: null for the same reason. agrees:0 was STRUCTURAL, not measured — the measurement could not validate the fix until the fix had already been applied.
fixDescription.fix: The expected issuer is now designated from the crosswalk's own CIK partition, which is derived from SEC's ticker file and therefore exists on a completely empty database. identifier_index is a cross-check, never the primary source.
algorithm: 1. SEC's ticker file assigns each symbol to exactly one CIK, partitioning the security nodes into per-CIK cohorts. No name matching anywhere.
2. A CIK's candidate issuer nodes are whatever its cohort's live links already point at.

3. A candidate is DISQUALIFIED if it holds a security SEC assigns to another CIK (holds-securities-of-another-cik) or if its fan-out exceeds the tickers SEC lists for the CIK (exceeds-sec-ticker-bound) — the same two computable rules issuer_fanout_violations enforces. Designating a collapsed node would bless the 183-security collapse, so designation and guardrail cannot disagree by construction.
4. The surviving candidate holding the most cohort members wins; tie-break on the lowest node id, so designation is deterministic.

5. An explicit identifier_index cik row wins when one exists, and concurrence with the cohort inference is reported either way (concurs / differs / cohort-inconclusive / no-index-row). On a clean database there are none and the measurement still works.
fixDescription.purity: designate_expected_issuers() takes the already-fetched (security_node_id, issuer_node_id) link pairs, touches no database, and never names an edge type. The trust boundary's single sanctioned read therefore stays the only place that query lives, and tests/test_issuer_link_trust.py is untouched and unweakened — TRUSTED_MATCH_METHODS is still ('cik-exact',) and app/securities/issuer_links.py is not modified by this PR.
fixDescription.semanticsMadeExplicit: agrees now means the existing link ALREADY GROUPS the security the way SEC's CIK partition does — the rebuild would not move it. It does NOT mean the link is trusted: a legacy edge carries no match_method, so trusted_issuer_links() still excludes it, and a test pins that so the two facts cannot blur. The report states two bases: disagreement_counts measures GROUPING against the crosswalk partition, planned measures what an --apply would actually WRITE (still a mint through identifier_index, because that is what resolve_issuer does).

fixDescription.secondDefectFoundWhileMeasuring: The first re-run reported cohort_size 99 for a CIK whose SEC ticker bound is 27. I checked the obvious explanation first and it was WRONG: duplicate security nodes per ticker account for only 11 extra nodes across 9,981 distinct symbols (max 2 nodes for any one symbol), so duplication could not produce 99. The real cause was that _symbol_by_security_node had no status filter and counted the 25,926 MERGED security nodes alongside the 9,992 active ones. A merged node is superseded (canonical() redirects reads to its survivor), so its stale links must not define the current grouping. Fixed in commit a2f5523: the designator reasons over active securities only, matching _security_nodes, and applies that definition to BOTH the cohorts and the purity test. links_skipped_not_active_securities makes the exclusion visible rather than silent.
fixDescription.secondDefectVerification: After the correction: BANK OF MONTREAL cohort_size 26 against bound 27 (was 99), JPMORGAN CHASE 2 against 9, BARCLAYS BANK 7 against 9 — all sane. links_skipped_not_active_securities is 0, which PROVES the correction fixed a reporting artifact without moving the measurement: agrees/disagrees/no_opinion are 44/103/8187 both before and after it.

remaining: THE HEADLINE FINDING, and it is not what the numbers first suggest: only 15 of 188 in-scope CIKs have an existing issuer node clean enough to designate. 173 are mint-required. So the legacy graph agrees with SEC's partition on 44 of 147 judgeable links (30%) and is structurally unusable for the other 70%.

OPERATOR RULING OWED — ADOPTION. adoptable_ciks is 15: those CIKs already have an existing issuer node that matches SEC's partition and is clean by the guardrail's computable rules, yet --apply would MINT A SECOND node for each, leaving two issuer nodes for the same real issuer. Adopting the existing node (claiming the CIK on it, which is purely additive: one identifier_index row) is the better graph but it hands a legacy name-derived node an authoritative identity. I did NOT change apply's behaviour and did NOT add an --adopt flag, because an unexercised write path is worse than an explicit open question. The count is now in the report so the ruling can be made with numbers.

OPERATOR RULING OWED — the 12-of-40 cik-split-across-issuer-nodes cases. ProShares Trust II and BANK OF MONTREAL each have their ticker family spread across 5 issuer nodes. Designation picks the node holding the most cohort members, which is deterministic but arbitrary in the sense that merging the 5 (merge_links already exists for exactly this) would be the real fix. The rebuild deliberately does not merge.

The 28-of-40 cik-has-no-clean-issuer-node cases are driven by exceeds-sec-ticker-bound, and the pattern is worth a ruling of its own: the nodes hold one SEC-recognised symbol plus dozens of symbols SEC does not list (e.g. iShares MSCI USA Size Factor ETF: 92 securities, 91 unrecognised, bound 2). I verified this is NOT a node-duplication artifact — only 11 symbols in the whole active master have more than one node. It is the foreign-line cohort colliding with US ETF issuers under fuzzy name match, which is the same root as the 914 unbounded-fanout nodes and is not fixable by a SEC CIK crosswalk.

Migration 0058 remains UNAPPLIED and I did not apply it. It is deploy-coupled (alembic upgrade head runs inside the deploy scripts) so it rides the next deploy in a soak-safe window. Note that the TW-32 fix means the measurement no longer DEPENDS on 0058 being applied — that was the point.
--apply was never run and is not authorized by this dispatch. The plan is unchanged and purely additive: 188 issuer nodes to create, 268 links to create, 0 to retire.

The report's samples are capped at sample_limit (40 used). The 103 disagreements and 935 guardrail violations exist in full only in the container report, which was deleted per the cleanup constraint.
